title: K-injective representative of the unit--Leray abutment map
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a scheme morphism, $K,L$ arbitrary complexes of abelian étale sheaves on $X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $v:f^{-1}K\to L$ a chain map [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $\rho:K\to I$ and $\sigma:L\to J$ be K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Suppose $j:f^{-1}I\to J$ satisfies $j\circ f^{-1}(\rho)\simeq\sigma\circ v$, and let $w:\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(Y,J)$ have components the sectionwise inverse-image unit followed by $\Gamma(j)$. For every integer $n$, the map $e_\rho^{-1}H^n(w)e_\sigma$, using the canonical resolution comparisons [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation], equals $H^n(R\Gamma_X(\eta_f);\lambda_f;R\Gamma_Y(v))$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Here $\eta_f$ is the unit of the derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunction and $\lambda_f$ is the canonical Leray isomorphism. This statement involves no filtration or spectral sequence.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-unit-leray to I=ρ.complex and J=σ.complex. This identifies the localized sectionwise w, conjugated by the K-injective right-derived comparison isomorphisms, with the unit--Leray map followed by the localized j.

Form the natural transformation β=RΓ_X(η_f) followed by λ_f. Naturality at Q(ρ.map) moves the source resolution map through β. Naturality of upperStar.mapDerivedCategoryFactors then replaces D(f inverse image)(Qρ) followed by the factorization at I with the factorization at K followed by Q(f inverse image(ρ)). Localize hj with DerivedCategory.Q_map_eq_of_homotopy to replace Q(f inverse image(ρ));Q(j) by Q(v);Q(σ.map). Cancel Q(σ.map) with its inverse. This gives a.hom;Q(w);b.inv=β_K;RΓ_Y(factors_K;Qv), where a and b are the resolution comparison isomorphisms before homology.

Apply DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor in degree n. Naturality of homologyFunctorFactors rewrites H(Qw) between its canonical comparison isomorphisms as HomologicalComplex.homologyMap w n. Unfold resolutionEtaleCohomologyIso: its inverse is H(a.hom) followed by the source homology factor, and its hom is the inverse target factor followed by H(b.inv). The middle factor and its inverse cancel, and functoriality gives H(a.hom;Qw;b.inv). Substitute the derived equality from step 2 and expand β to obtain exactly the required equation.
